title: py8dis JSON output, version 1
description: The finished disassembly as data, written by py8dis with --json FILE (with or without -o for the asm). See docs/json-format.md. Optional keys are left out when empty. A reader should ignore keys it doesn't know: they may be added without changing the version.

assembler.description: The assembler the asm was written for (as given by the assembler's get_name()). Every 'text' field uses its syntax.

loads.description: The files loaded with load() or load_prg(), in the order loaded: the filename as given, the binary addresses the data is loaded at, where in the file the data loaded starts (if not at the start), and whether it's a PRG file loaded with load_prg().

moves.description: The move() commands, in the order made. Move 0 (no move) isn't listed.

constants.description: The constant() definitions, in the order the asm defines them.

text.description: The value as the asm shows it.

memory_regions.description: The memory regions in effect (the CPU's, acorn.py's and the control file's, after any renaming or removal), by start address then size.

subroutines.description: The subroutine() definitions in the loaded data, or whose names the asm uses, by runtime address.

labels.description: Every address with a name, inside or outside the loaded data, by runtime address.

items.description: One for each instruction or piece of data, by binary address. Together they cover the loaded data exactly.

range_boundaries.description: The places at the start or end of a range of the output (the loaded data, or a move's data) where the asm defines labels or gives comments, with no item for them: e.g. the label for the source of a move's data, which the asm defines just before the moved code. By binary address, then move.

labels.description: The names the asm defines here, in order.

comments.description: The comments here, in output order.

label_addr.description: A label's runtime address: this can be 65536, just past the top of memory (e.g. pydis_end, for data that ends there).

move_id.description: The move (see 'moves'); left out when 0, i.e. not moved.

range.description: Addresses from 'start' up to, but not including, 'end'.

text.description: As written in the control file (or by py8dis), before word wrapping.

autogenerated.description: True if py8dis wrote it, e.g. 'referenced 2 times by'.

kind.description: 'overlapping' for an instruction found while tracing that overlaps the code or data there; 'raw' for text added with annotate(), output as it is. Left out for an ordinary comment.

registers.description: A description of each register, e.g. {"a": "the character"}.

names.description: The label's names, in the order the asm defines them.

autogenerated.description: Made up by py8dis (e.g. l2000), rather than given by the control file, acorn.py or a label maker hook.

definition.description: Where the asm defines it: 'inline' at its address, 'relative' as an offset from the label at the start of the item it's inside (e.g. l2001 = c2000+1), 'memory_locations' as 'name = value' at the top, or 'none' if the asm doesn't need it.

memory_region.description: For a 'memory_locations' definition, the heading it's under (the memory region's name, or 'Other'), if there are headings.

local_names.description: Names given with local_label(), each used only by the code in its range of binary addresses (from 'start' up to, but not including, 'end'). The asm defines them under 'Memory locations'.

output_name.description: The name the asm uses, if different (e.g. temp_2 when temp is used for another address).

memory_region.description: The 'Memory locations' heading it's under, if there are headings.

expressions.description: Expressions naming this address, given with expr_label(), e.g. table+1.

references.description: The instructions and data that refer to this address (each the binary address of the instruction, or of the byte or word, with the runtime address it runs at), by binary address.

expr.description: An expression: the text as in the asm, and its tree.

oneOf.description: A number, with how it's shown (if py8dis knows): 'decimal', 'signed_decimal', 'hex' (2 or 4 digits as needed), 'hex2' or 'hex4' (that many digits), 'binary', 'picture_binary' or 'char'.

A label: its runtime address, and the name used here. The name is usually one of the label's names, but can be an expression relative to another label (e.g. brkv+1), as py8dis sometimes names an address.
An expression written as a string in the control file, which py8dis doesn't parse.
A unary operator, using py8dis's names: '<' (low byte), '>' (high byte), 'NOT', or another given to make_op1().
A binary operator, using py8dis's names: '+', '-', '*', 'DIV', 'MOD', 'AND', 'OR', 'EOR', '<<', '>>', or another given to make_op2().

cpu_state.description: What py8dis knows for certain about the registers and flags once the instruction has run (as set_show_cpu_state(True) shows): null where unknown. For the 6502 and 65C02: a, x, y and the flags n, v, d, i, z, c. For the 8080: a, b, c, d, e, h, l, sp and the flags s, z, ac (auxiliary carry), p, cy.

labels.description: The names the asm defines at this item, in order.

comments.description: The comments at this item, in output order.

text.description: The instruction or data as in the asm, without its layout: one string for each line.

mnemonic.description: instruction: as in the asm. (For the 8080, without any register operands, which are in 'text'.)

mode.description: instruction: the addressing mode. 6502/65C02: implied, accumulator, immediate, zp, zp_x, zp_y, zp_indirect, zp_x_indirect, zp_indirect_y, absolute, absolute_x, absolute_y, indirect, absolute_x_indirect, relative. 8080: implied, immediate, immediate16, address.

operand.description: instruction: the operand's value (an address, or an immediate value), with its expression.

target.description: instruction: for a branch, jump or call, the runtime address it goes to.

undocumented.description: instruction: true for an undocumented opcode (e.g. the 8080's &CB, which runs as JMP), which the asm writes as data bytes. 'mnemonic' and 'mode' are those of the instruction it runs as.

cycles.description: instruction: the cycles taken, as set_show_cycles(True) shows them, e.g. "2/3" for a 6502 branch (not taken, or taken), or "5/11" for an 8080 conditional return (or "halts" for the 6502's undocumented JAM).

exprs.description: bytes, words: the expression for each value given with expr(), or null. Left out if there are none.

encoding.description: string: its text encoding, if not ASCII (see config.set_text_encoding()).
